units.source_text: [\[9\]](#part1330.html#w9) 京中武官有左右近卫、左右卫门、左右兵卫，共称六卫府。

en.t: Among the military officials in the capital were the Left and Right Palace Guards, the Left and Right Gate Guards, and the Left and Right Soldiers' Guards, together known as the Six Guard Offices.

units.source_text: 近卫府负责警卫皇宫之门内，左右近卫府的长官称大将，次官称中将、少将，三等官称将监，四等官称将曹。

en.t: The Palace Guard Office was responsible for guarding the area inside the palace gates; the chiefs of the Left and Right Palace Guard Offices were called generals, their deputy officers were called middle generals and minor generals, the third-rank officers were called guard inspectors, and the fourth-rank officers were called guard clerks.

units.source_text: 左右近卫大将、中将等，略称左近大将、右近中将、右大将、左中将等。

en.t: Titles such as Left and Right Palace Guard general and middle general were abbreviated as Left Palace Guard general, Right Palace Guard middle general, Right general, Left middle general, and the like.
Middle generals and minor generals were also called assistant officers and aides.

units.source_text: 卫门府负责警卫皇宫之门外，左右卫门府的长官称督，次官称佐、权佐，三等官称大尉、少尉。

en.t: The Gate Guard Office was responsible for guarding the area outside the palace gates; the chiefs of the Left and Right Gate Guard Offices were called commanders, their deputy officers were called assistants and provisional assistants, and the third-rank officers were called senior lieutenants and junior lieutenants.

units.source_text: 卫门府又特称韧负司，其佐、尉称韧负佐、韧负尉。

en.t: The Gate Guard Office was also specially called the Yuge Office, and its assistants and lieutenants were called Yuge assistants and Yuge lieutenants.

units.source_text: 兵卫府负责警卫皇宫之门外，并巡检京中。

en.t: The Soldiers' Guard Office was responsible for guarding the area outside the palace gates and also patrolled the capital.
Its official titles were the same as those of the Gate Guard Office.
